P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title, so P1a is N/A. Positioning was established ('my name is Andrew. I'm a senior advisor with Trevor. So you're in good hands') and the open question was run cleanly — 'tell me man, what brought you here and how can we actually help you?' No four-part frame was set and no frame agreement was sought, which matters here: the prospect reached minute 39 without any idea a price of this size was coming, and said so.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in this batch. Height was asked directly and target weight was asked ('what weight would you like to achieve?'), though age and current weight were volunteered rather than asked, hence partial on P2a. Occupation and its desk-bound nature were volunteered and then confirmed rather than asked, hence partial on P2b. Chronic conditions were asked explicitly ('do you have, like, any other, maybe chronic conditions, something like that?'), injuries were asked and probed for current impact ('Is that showing up on a daily basis right now?'), the training week was asked ('what's your routine, like typical week look like in terms of training?'), diet was asked, and sleep and energy were both asked in one well-formed move ('How's your sleep levels? Like, you had to scale it from 1 to 10, when you wake up, how do you feel?') with the follow-up 'Is that affecting your work also?'. The one real gap is that a physician's recommendation to start cholesterol medication was volunteered at 00:06:25 and never followed up.

P3.evidence: Excellent depth work. The bridge landed — 'in your own words, what's the biggest reason you actually want to get stronger and lose some weight?' — and was followed by the emotional probe 'when you say it actually, like, out loud, that you feel that you fell off during those years, like, how that actually sits with you?'. The possibility question ran ('when you actually will get in better shape... What new possibilities open up?'), the impact question ran ('How your wife would actually react to your change?'), and the rep drove all the way through to identity and self-trust — 'keeping the promise to yourself that you're capable, is that it?' followed by 'And why is that so important?'. The reflect-back at 00:18:19 is a model of the move: 'when you're saying that basically you want to level up your life, and it's not only for you, but it's also for your wife... That you're again the same Daniel that it was seven years ago.' P3c is a miss under the volunteered-information rule — hiking and the Appalachian Trail came out entirely on the prospect's initiative.

P4.evidence: The root-cause question was asked well — 'let me ask you something honestly, like, what do you feel like has actually been stopping you from fixing this up to this point?' — and the prospect named his own gap: energy, excuses, and 'I don't have the knowledge of what to do'. But the past-attempts half of the phase was never run. The prospect volunteered 'I've done workout plans before and they've, you know, I've seen success years ago' and the rep did not ask what they were, what happened, or why they stopped. That is exactly the material the consequence frame and the price conversation would have needed.

P5.evidence: The consequence question was asked — 'If nothing actually changes, and we will be having these conversations a year from now, how do you think, where does this go?' — but the prospect deflected into process ('I gotta reevaluate... consider my schedule') and the rep let it stand. The follow-up 'how would that affect your work, your relationship, your health, your energy levels?' was then answered as an upside ('I think working out and losing the weight will benefit everything'), which is the opposite of a consequence, and again went unredirected. No 'willing to settle for that', no 'why not'. The nearest line-in-the-sand was 'is there anything outside of yourself that would actually stop you from committing to this journey?' The cost of inaction was never made to bite, and that is visible forty minutes later when $6,000 lands against nothing.

P6.evidence: Both moves run properly and in order, before any price: 'if you had the right training, the simple nutrition, and real accountability from Trevor and all built around your life, do you agree that you would get to your goal, the Daniel 2.0?' then 'if we can figure out the details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become that Daniel?' — answered 'For sure, man. Yeah, 100%.' The rep only moved to the investment after that.

P11.evidence: The offer was presented and declined on price. Payment and onboarding were never reachable, so the phase drops out of the denominator rather than scoring as a miss.

objection_plays.detail: Ran roughly half the play and then inverted one of its core moves. Present and correct: the isolation ('Just finances aside, is there anything else that would be keeping you from being 100% in on this?'), the should/how reframe ('you're not in a, should I do it? You're in more of a, how do I make it work'), the cost-of-inaction question, and the permission question ('would you be open to actually have an honest conversation about the finances and how we can actually make it work for you?'). Inverted: the script's 'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' became 'we don't have set payment plans for customers. Most of them, they just take it upfront' — the break-it-up option was withheld rather than offered. Of the six financial-picture questions only cash on hand was asked (refused) and credit cards touched on; monthly surplus after bills, total available credit per card, used versus available, and investments were never asked. When the prospect declined the cash question the rep challenged the refusal rather than moving to the next question, and the play never recovered.

Two script gaps surfaced. First, a prospect who is bought in on the product and genuinely cannot reach $6,000 — the script's only answer is to establish capacity to pay, and when capacity is genuinely absent there is nothing scripted between $6,000 one-on-one and walking away. The rep improvised a $200/month community downsell that appears nowhere in the playbook. Second, a prospect who refuses financial disclosure on principle ('no one's ever asked me that question ever') — there is no scripted recovery for a declined open-wallet conversation, and the rep pushed instead.

notes: The first thirty-eight minutes are the best-run discovery in this batch — P2, P3 and P6 are close to textbook, and he earned a clear 100% before naming a price. Everything after 00:39 is the coaching material. Three specific corrections: when a prospect declines the cash-on-hand question, move on to available credit and monthly surplus rather than challenging the refusal; do not propose buy-now-pay-later lending to someone who has just disclosed he is paying down credit card debt; and P5 was the phase that would have carried the price, so a deflected consequence answer needs redirecting, not accepting. Worth noting the rep did not discount the core offer, which is the right instinct — but the $200/month improvisation is still an unauthorised price.
